body.observations: The only run so far is r001 with all defaults (weightUdp=0.5, queuePkts=100, TcpCubic, duration=10, seed=1): udp_goodput_bps=300003200, tcp_goodput_bps=482667053, udp_loss_frac=0.0, drops_band1=77, tcp_retrans=77, link_util=0.807098. TCP goodput is close to half of 1Gbps after packet overhead, suggesting the scheduler may be giving TCP roughly its configured (1-weightUdp) share and not fully using UDP's unused share. UDP is lossless at weightUdp=0.5. The goal is to maximize tcp_goodput_bps subject to udp_loss_frac <= 0.01, so the key unknown is the minimum weightUdp that keeps UDP loss below 1% and how tcp_goodput changes as weightUdp is lowered.

body.explanation: The scheduler's configured UDP share is the dominant control. With the default weightUdp=0.5, TCP receives only about half the link and gets 482.667 Mbps even though the link is not fully utilized. Reducing weightUdp lets TCP use more of the 1 Gbps link; at weightUdp=0.32 TCP reaches 656.426 Mbps, and near the UDP-loss threshold TCP reaches about 671.5-671.9 Mbps with link_util about 1.0. The UDP flow needs slightly more than 0.3026 of the link because of packetization/scheduling effects; below the threshold its queue overflows and udp_loss_frac exceeds 0.01. Queue size affects the UDP-loss margin: queuePkts=100 becomes unacceptable just below about 0.30295, queuePkts=400 allows about 0.30285, and queuePkts=600 allowed 0.30265 in the tested runs. queuePkts=1000 reduced TCP goodput at weightUdp=0.32, indicating bufferbloat or scheduling delay, so 600 is the best tested queue size. TCP congestion control does not materially increase goodput once the TCP share is filled: TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, and TcpBic all reached the same 671.533 Mbps at weightUdp=0.303 and queuePkts=100, while TcpBbr and TcpVegas were much lower. Therefore the constrained optimum is to set weightUdp as low as possible while keeping UDP loss at or below 1%, with queuePkts=600 and a loss-based TCP variant; the best tested such point is weightUdp=0.30265, queuePkts=600, TcpCubic.
body.holds_when: The link is 1 Gbps with 50 us one-way delay, UDP sends 1400-byte packets at 300 Mbps, TCP has 1 MB buffers and a full segment fills one 1500-byte packet, the scheduler behaves as observed in these runs, seed=1, and duration=10 s. It also assumes the UDP loss constraint is exactly udp_loss_frac <= 0.01 over the measured window.
body.breaks_when: It would change if the UDP rate, UDP packet size, link rate, link delay, TCP buffers, scheduler policy, seed, or measurement duration change enough to move the UDP-loss threshold; if a stricter UDP-loss target is required; if queuePkts is increased too far and bufferbloat reduces TCP goodput; or if TcpBbr or TcpVegas is used instead of a loss-based variant.

claims.text: TCP goodput is primarily limited by the scheduler's configured TCP share; lowering weightUdp below 0.5 increases TCP goodput substantially while UDP loss can remain acceptable near 0.32.
The UDP-loss constraint binds near weightUdp about 0.30265-0.30295, depending on queue size; below the threshold udp_loss_frac exceeds 0.01.

queuePkts=600 is the best tested queue size for this constrained optimum: very small queues do not improve TCP goodput, queuePkts=1000 reduces TCP goodput, and queuePkts=400/600 improve the UDP-loss margin enough to permit a lower weightUdp.
Loss-based TCP variants fill the configured TCP share and give the same TCP goodput at the tested operating point, while TcpBbr and TcpVegas underfill the link and reduce TCP goodput.
The best tested setting satisfying udp_loss_frac <= 0.01 is weightUdp=0.30265, queuePkts=600, TcpCubic, duration=10, seed=1, with tcp_goodput_bps=671870707 and udp_loss_frac=0.009811.

Whether the optimum is robust across other seeds and longer measurement durations.
